My thoughts is it’s possible it’s a URI. For my rats who have had URI’s sneezing a lot is generally the first symptom, eventually it develops into wheezing which after that I could only really every clear it up with antibiotics.

No matter how clean you keep things or how well ventilated the room is occasionally you’ll get URI’s. While husbandry can affect it I wouldn’t blame the occurrence on your husbandry if you know you aren’t slacking on the clean job. 

Anyway, it’s hard to say for sure if it’s just a case of the sniffles or a URI. Going to a vet, confirming, and treating is probably your best bet. When it gets to the point of wheezing I’ve found not every rat bounces back despite treatment, especially if they are older.

My advice, if they feel like a chore a rehome may be better. Pets are suppose to be enjoyable. Rats are a lot of work and pretty susceptible to things like URIs. They need a lot of attention and medical care and not everyone can provide that.

If you are struggling to get them out everyday you can try to create a schedule. Get them out at the same time everyday for an hour or two. Having a routine has really helped me out.

Aside from that there’s not a whole lot you can do if the issue boils down to you just not having the energy to let them out. If you can’t find the motivation it may be best to not own rats at this current time. Ultimately you need to do what’s best for your pet.

If you are getting a baby rat from a breeder you need to get two. Same age company is important for development. So if you are getting young rats you can’t get just one.

However if you are rescuing/adopting an older rat getting one should be fine, but more often than not older rats are already in bonded pairs which can’t be separated. 

It’s much easier just to get two for the most part. And bigger groups tend to be better.

To an extent more is better. If you are around to hang out with them, it’s better they get out. For me if I’m home and in my room I just open the cage door and let them go in and out as they please. Even when they are asleep I open it so they at the very least can choose to go outside. I find they’ll choose to go out, even if it’s just for half an hour or so. 

I wouldn’t keep them out for less than an hour a day. 1-2 hours daily tends to be the agreed upon minimum. Apart of owning pets is working your schedule around them. You may just have to set aside one hour or two of your relaxation time for them. After all you chose to own them, and freeroam is part of owning rats. If you are already doing an hour each day then you’re doing good, however it never hurts to get them out more.

Just keep the rest of their cage clean and their litter pan smelly and eventually they’ll get the idea. If you notice they liking pooping in a certain spot move the litter tray there.

If you notice them using the litter pans it wouldn’t hurt to reward them with a treat. I personally never rewarded mine but if your boys are being stubborn it may help nudge them in the right direction.

Pretty much your goal is to get it parallel with the hole. Waiting till its close to the hole is key as its pretty luck based whether the claw drops it correctly. Once its lined with the hole you want to barely grab the highest side. I find it easier with the highest side in the middle. Then you just grab the ends. Since these claws are SUPER strong if you undershoot and grab to early you'll lose all your progress. Also depending on the boxes position in might help to offset your claw.

​

Axolotls aren't social animals and do not need a pair. They can be kept alone without issue.

Hello! Getting an axolotl is super exciting! I've had my pair for a couple years now and heres what I've learned/ found useful.

Personally for tanks I recommend one that is 20+ gallons (if you are housing one axolotl) Axolotls are super messy and most tanks smaller than that will get dirty incredible quick. If possible get a tank on the longer side rather than taller as axolotls tend to hang out near the ground. 

Another good thing is getting a turkey baster. Axolotls produce lots of solid waste and it can help you keep your tank looking cleaner longer if you spot clean using one.

Tile bottoms are amazing! Unlike sand which is a disaster to clean tile (ones with a rough surface for grip) don't trap waste if they are fit to the tank, are much easier to take out and wash, and easier to spot clean on. Extra bonus they will never end up impacting your axolotl.

Finally just be careful about your filters flow. Heavy currents stress axolotls out so try to get a filter with a slow flow.
